name: Hana Solberg
life: Hana sees the viaduct from ladders, inspection platforms and the driver's seat. She didn't see the lighthouse in the mirror herself until a maintenance passenger showed it to her on a perfectly uneventful crossing. People around Harbour Bakery know Hana by a small Saturday habit. Hana buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: The best view is from the passenger side at the crest. He had crossed it eight thousand times without seeing the lighthouse in the mirror. I asked the driver to give him that seat.
appearance: Hana has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Hana looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Hana is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Hana asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To show the retiring driver the lighthouse in the passenger mirror.
family: Elizabeth Yoon is Hana’s second cousin. Hana picks the meeting place. Elizabeth sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Saturday keys*, Elizabeth says, “I used to hide my key in a shoe. After losing my home I hate the idea somebody else carries it.”
connections: Andre Bell. One remembers being given a lift in a crisis. The other wants this final lift to include the view at the bridge crest.

reactions.situation: The old driver wants to change the farewell route
reactions.response: Hana takes the changed route seriously and checks who needs to know the new return time.
